queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.

hook.speaker: Krishna
hook.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
hook.sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः । स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥
hook.line: Devoted to your own work, you reach fulfilment. Here's how.
hook.translation: Each person, devoted to his own work, attains perfection. Hear how one devoted to his own work finds perfection.
hook.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
hook.misuse: Not 'stay in the job your community or birth assigned'. 'Your own work' means the work that fits your nature.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
alternates.sanskrit: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥
alternates.line: Like smoke over fire, dust on a mirror, desire covers your clear sight.
alternates.translation: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb, so is this wisdom covered by desire.
alternates.why: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

prasang.title: Restraining desire
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasang.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
alternates.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
alternates.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
alternates.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.

words.en: cause of the fruit of action

alternates.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
alternates.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, where everything has stopped and Arjuna has refused to fight. Krishna tells him that every person reaches perfection by doing the work that fits their own nature. He says that work done as an offering, with its flaws and all, is the true path to fulfilment. The idea is that you do not need to be perfect or have a flawless plan. You only need to find the work that is yours and give it your full attention.
verse.for_you: You are building something of your own and raising your children. You have made your choice. The hard part is the morning when the work stops feeling exciting. Devote yourself to your own work, flaws and all, as an offering. Your own path beats another's.
verse.try_today: Choose one small task at work and give it your full attention today.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the start of what is yours to build.
asks: How do I know if a craving is a signal or just noise?
How do I stay devoted when the excitement fades?

verse.speaker: Janaka
verse.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
verse.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
verse.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
verse.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
verse.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.meaning: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof, overhears wandering sages singing about the self. He questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away. He gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches. The verse says that all those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes. You don't have to leave your life to change it.
verse.for_you: You are building your own work and raising your children, and the mind wants to clutch at every result. The verse says that the mind that clings to fortune turns it into trouble. The mind that accepts misfortune turns it into fortune.
verse.try_today: Do one task at your work without holding on to the outcome.
verse.scene_line: You are on your own roof, and the doorkeeper calls you to your duties.
asks: How do I know when I am clinging to the work?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.

words.en: here no stepping back, no destruction

verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.for_you: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: ऐहिकः प्राक्तनं हन्ति प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनं बलात् । सर्वदा पुरुषस्पन्दस्तत्रानुद्वेगवाञ्जयी ॥
verse.line: Today's effort and yesterday's keep wrestling. Whoever stays calm through it wins.
verse.translation: Present effort overcomes the past, and the past can overpower the present. It is always a contest of human striving, and the one who stays calm wins.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha tells Rama that the present and the past are always wrestling. Today's effort shapes tomorrow, just as yesterday's effort shaped today. What people call fate is only the fruit of past striving. It is a contest of human effort, and the one who stays calm through it wins.
verse.for_you: You are building something of your own and raising children at the same time. The past effort that brought you here is wrestling with the effort you need now. Do not let the memory of what you have already done weigh down the work ahead. Stay calm with the process.
verse.try_today: Notice one task you usually rush through and slow it down.

verse.speaker: Angada
verse.setting: The monkeys searching for Sita are exhausted and failing; young Angada rallies them.
verse.sanskrit: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥
verse.line: Keep working and the results will come. Sink into despair and it is hard to get back up.
verse.translation: Those who keep working surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
verse.why: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

prasang.title: The missed deadline
prasang.summary: The southern search party loses time in a magic cave and misses Sugriva's deadline. Angada rallies them once, then despairs, fearing punishment and certain he will be blamed. Hanuman reasons with him to return.
prasang.story_hook: They came out of the cave to find that spring had already come, and their deadline had gone.
prasang.lesson: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

verse.meaning: The monkeys searching for Sita are exhausted and have lost precious time. They have missed the deadline. Young Angada, their leader, feels the weight of this failure and despairs. He believes their punishment is certain and that all is lost. Hanuman speaks to him and reminds him that the search must continue. The verse says that those who keep working will see the results, but once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again. It is a warning against giving up when the path ahead is dark.
verse.for_you: You are in the middle of building something that belongs to you. There are days when the effort feels heavy and the future is unclear. The work is yours, and the craving to see it finished is real.
verse.try_today: Return to one small part of the work that still holds your attention.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verse.sanskrit: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verse.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
verse.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.for_you: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.

story.title: Hanuman's leap
story.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
story.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
story.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

anchor.speaker: Beings of the sky
anchor.setting: Having outwitted two monsters mid-flight, Hanuman is praised by those watching from the sky.
anchor.sanskrit: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्य स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥
anchor.line: Steadiness, clear sight, good judgement and skill. With these four, you won't sink at work.
anchor.translation: Whoever has these four, as you do, chief of monkeys, never sinks in his work: steadiness, clear sight, judgement and skill.
anchor.why: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

prasang.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.
